home.originQuote: "In Lobitos we make ponchos that carry the spirit of the Andes. Every piece is woven by hands that have inherited generations of tradition, using natural wool from the mountains. It's more than something warm to wear: it's a connection to the land, to our culture, and to the kind of warmth only handmade work can give."

cause.seoDescription: How can we make the world a little better? Local production, our grandmothers, sustainable tourism and inspiring others: the four things we care about most at Lobitos Ponchos.
cause.title:
How can we
make the world
a little better?
cause.lead: We know we can't change the whole world in one go. But we believe that if each of us changes a little bit of what's around us, together, over time, we can make a big difference.
cause.intro: We've asked ourselves a lot of questions about what we stand for and what we want Lobitos Ponchos to become. These are the four things that matter most to us:

c1.title:
Local production
& the environment
c1.photoAlt: The Lobitos Ponchos stand on the beach with a sign that reads «Diseña tu propio Surf Poncho!» (Design your own surf poncho!)
c1.lead: In Peru, many people feel they have to move to Lima to find a better future. We want to create new opportunities right here, and show that not everything has to be made in the capital.
c1.p1: We want to step away from fast fashion. We'd rather make one piece you truly love, that you can make your own and want to wear for years, than lots of things that don't mean much.
c1.p2: We also turn our fabric scraps into accessories and other products, so as little as possible goes to waste.
c1.p3: We know there's still more we can do. In the future we'd love to work with more and more sustainable materials and keep finding new ways to lighten our footprint.
c1.collabLead: Got an idea? Know a material we could use? Want to help us find new solutions?
c1.collabText: We're always open to learning and working together.

c2.title: Our grandmothers
c2.photoAlt: One of our grandmothers with a visitor, showing Lobitos Ponchos pouches in front of her sewing machine
c2.lead: It's easy to forget how much our elders are worth: their knowledge, their experience, and everything they still have to share.
c2.p1: With Lobitos Ponchos, our grandmothers can work comfortably from home, bring their know-how to make every product better, and spend more time with their grandsons, Kevyn and Iván.
c2.p2: They also get to meet the people who come all the way to their homes to see how their poncho is made. These are encounters that would probably never have happened otherwise.

c3.title: Sustainable tourism
c3.photoAlt: Local kids and visitors in ponchos on a fishing boat pulled up on the beach in Lobitos
c3.lead: Many visitors to Lobitos move mostly between their hotel, the beach and the usual sights, without ever really meeting the people who built this town.
c3.p1: With Lobitos Ponchos we want to create experiences that bring visitors closer to village life: to its families, its history, and a community that has lived from fishing and the sea for generations.
c3.highlight: Through this project we've already seen friendships grow between people from completely different cultures and walks of life.

c4.title: Inspiring others
c4.quote: Maybe this is our biggest dream: to show that you really can start with very little.
c4.p1: We want to show that young people, grandmothers, locals and people who came here from other countries can work side by side. And that it feels amazing to be part of building something that wants to grow in a more mindful, sustainable way.
c4.p2: We hope our excitement for creating, collaborating and backing local projects is contagious.
c4.photoAlt: Collage of young people from Lobitos

closing.title: Because maybe changing the world doesn't start with trying to change everything.
closing.text: Maybe it starts with caring for, and changing, a little bit of the place around you.

team.seoDescription: The hands behind every piece: meet the grandmothers and young people of Lobitos who make each poncho by hand.
team.title:
The hands
behind
every piece
team.lead: We're a group of people who believe in craftsmanship, in working with our hands, and in the stories that live inside every piece.
team.closingTitle: Ponchos that hold on to tradition. Fabrics made to last.

people.label: 01 — Founder
people.name: Esmérita "Mery" Eche Periche
people.bio: Esmérita is 70 and has spent her whole life in Lobitos. She learned to sew on a machine from her mother and made it her craft from a very young age. Today she's returned to that passion, bringing a lifetime of sewing experience to the workshop and shaping every piece with hands that have never stopped carrying tradition forward.

people.label: 02 — Master artisan
people.name: Irma Bancayan Eche
people.bio: Kevyn's grandmother, born and raised in Lobitos and still living here. Irma has been sewing and making things by hand since she was 10. She overlocks the edges and joins the pieces together, the step that gives each poncho its final shape before it goes to quality check.

people.label: 03 — Production
people.name: Kevyn Abad (19)
people.bio: Born and raised in Lobitos, Kevyn is studying Hospitality and Restaurant Management. He takes the orders, measures customers, chooses the color combinations, and picks up, cuts and delivers the fabric to his grandmothers. He also checks the quality and hands over every finished poncho. He's the engine that connects the workshop with each customer. His goal: to support his grandmothers and pay for his studies.

people.label: 04 — Marketing & strategy
people.name: Kerstin Ulrich "Tiíta" (32)
people.bio: Born and raised in Switzerland to a Peruvian mother, Kerstin first came to Lobitos in 2018 as a volunteer with Waves Lobitos, and never quite left. She brings her love of photography to the project, sharing the story of Lobitos with the world without losing what makes it real. She's proud to be part of a team that is, above all, family.

people.label: 05 — Admin & community
people.name: Ivan Vite (20)
people.bio: Born and raised in Lobitos, Ivan is currently studying Environmental Engineering away from home. He keeps the admin side of the project running, making sure that behind every handmade piece there's also order, care and community.
